newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Skanska to reveal dividend plan in a month.
newsitem.headline: Skanska to reveal dividend plan in a month.

text.p: Swedish construction company Skanska AB said on Wednesday it would unveil within a month its plan to distribute eight to ten billion crowns to shareholders.
"Within a month we will come out with a decision. A unanimous board has decided to transfer eight to 10 billion crowns to shareholders," Skanska managing director Melker Schorling told a seminar.
A day earlier Skanska said it was studying how to best implement an additional transfer of this money to shareholders because its capital exceeded the requirements of its core business.
"We are now investigating the situation tax wise to find the best solution to minimise tax for our owners," said Schorling.
"When the dividend can occur is unclear, but our goal is as soon a possible...the dividend can be in lots or all at once," he added.

The transfer will be financed by Skanska's shareholdings in non-core operations. The two largest holdings are Skanska's 25.9 percent stake in engineer Sandvik and its 8.7 percent holding in rolling bearing company SKF.
The bourse portfolio was valued to 11.9 billion crowns at year-end 1996, with Sandvik worth 10.3 billion crowns and SKF 1.5 billion crowns.

The company would not confirm the details of the dividend, saying only: "To distribute the Sandvik shares to shareholders may be a solution...but the dividend is tax-wise a worse solution than a share redemption," Schorling said.
Schorling repeated that breaking up the company was not on the agenda, contrary to speculation.
"We have said that a spin-off of the properties division is not on the agenda. But we can divest parts of our holdings...We continue to work actively with our property portfolio," Schorling said.
